name: Bezalel (son of Uri, grandson of Hur)
title: Master Craftsman of the Tabernacle
summary: Bezalel was a gifted craftsman from the tribe of Judah chosen by God to lead the construction of the tabernacle and its holy articles. He was filled with God's Spirit and given wisdom, understanding, and knowledge in all kinds of craftsmanship. Bezalel represents the first biblical example of someone specifically mentioned as being filled with God's Spirit for artistic work.

keyEvents.title: God's Choice of Bezalel
keyEvents.description: God called Bezalel by name and filled him with His Spirit, wisdom, understanding, and knowledge to carry out artistic work with gold, silver, bronze, precious stones, and wood.

keyEvents.title: Collaboration with Oholiab
keyEvents.description: God gave Bezalel the assistant Oholiab from the tribe of Dan, and together they led the artistic work on the tabernacle.

keyEvents.title: Tasks Involving the Tabernacle's Articles
keyEvents.description: Bezalel was entrusted with making the tent of meeting, the ark of the covenant, the mercy seat, the altar, the priestly garments, and all the holy articles.

keyEvents.title: Moses Presents Bezalel to the People
keyEvents.description: Moses told the Israelites that the Lord had called Bezalel and equipped him with all the necessary skills for the sacred work.

keyEvents.title: The Execution of the Work
keyEvents.description: Bezalel and Oholiab, together with all the skilled craftsmen, carried out the work on the tabernacle exactly as the Lord had commanded Moses.

keyEvents.title: Bezalel Makes the Ark of the Covenant
keyEvents.description: Bezalel made the ark of the covenant from acacia wood and overlaid it with pure gold, and he crafted the mercy seat with cherubim from hammered gold.
